bottleneck.description: KAIST HUBO spinout, now 35%-owned by Samsung, with RB Series cobots and HUBO humanoid platform; competes with UR, Doosan, Techman, Fanuc CRX, ABB GoFa in cobots and with global humanoid pure-plays.

dependency.key_customers: Samsung Electronics (anchor), Korean industrial users, US distribution via Schaumburg, IL branch
dependency.key_suppliers: Vertical integration on actuators/encoders/controllers; harmonic reducer imports (Harmonic Drive Systems, Leader)

editorial.notes: Samsung's largest-shareholder backing provides capital and a likely flagship customer, but this is a downstream relationship, not an upstream bottleneck. The cobot market is structurally contested (Universal Robots, Doosan, Techman, JAKA, Han's Robot) with sub-50% Rainbow share even in Korea. Vertical integration on actuators/encoders is a cost story, not a sole-source moat for downstream customers. HUBO humanoid line is a research platform, not committed production. Despite the Samsung halo, the structural position remains LOW alongside other peer-competitive robot OEMs (Fanuc, ABB at LOW per anchors).
